title: NCBI genetic codes
description: NCBI translation tables. aminoAcids is the 64-character assignment string in the NCBI codon order (first base T,C,A,G outermost; second base next; third base innermost), i.e. the same order as the ncbieaa string in the NCBI genetic-code file. starts lists the documented initiation codons for the table; a codon absent from that list is not treated as an initiator.

codes.name: Standard
codes.notes: NCBI transl_table 1. The alternative initiators TTG and CTG are the ones NCBI lists for this table.

codes.name: Vertebrate Mitochondrial
codes.notes: NCBI transl_table 2. AGA and AGG are termination codons; TGA is Trp; ATA is Met.

codes.name: Yeast Mitochondrial
codes.notes: NCBI transl_table 3. CTN codons are Thr, TGA is Trp, ATA is Met. NCBI notes that CGA and CGC are absent in Saccharomyces cerevisiae; they are left as Arg here because that is what the published table string contains.

codes.name: Mold, Protozoan, Coelenterate Mitochondrial and Mycoplasma/Spiroplasma
codes.notes: NCBI transl_table 4. TGA is Trp; the amino-acid assignments are otherwise the standard ones.

codes.name: Invertebrate Mitochondrial
codes.notes: NCBI transl_table 5. AGA and AGG are Ser, TGA is Trp, ATA is Met.

codes.name: Bacterial, Archaeal and Plant Plastid
codes.notes: NCBI transl_table 11. Amino-acid assignments are identical to table 1; only the set of documented initiation codons differs.
